title: Vendor-agnostic automated PACE/multi-path transport orchestration and single-pane tactical NetOps for S6/G6 at brigade and below (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF)
problem: Brigade-and-below units now carry three to five transports (MANET, pLEO, GEO, private 5G, HF) but path selection/failover and network status are still executed by signal soldiers through separate vendor consoles and paper PACE plans, so applications stall during jamming or movement and link/spectrum/cyber awareness is manual and slow.

user.exact_role: Battalion/brigade S6 (signal officer) and the brigade/division NetOps cell (25-series signal soldiers, network technicians 255A/255N), plus platform/vehicle crews who physically switch transports; NGC2 transport-layer integrators on the vendor side
user.echelon: Battalion through division, with the operational pain concentrated at brigade and below where signal staff are smallest
organization_examples: 4th Infantry Division (NGC2 prototype, Ivy Sting/Ivy Mass)
III Armored Corps and I Corps (baseline NGC2 recipients 2026)
Expeditionary Signal Battalions-Enhanced (ESB-E) and division signal companies
NETCOM / Army CIO-G6 (Unified Network Plan 2.0 owner)
USSOCOM (TACLAN/SDN 'King for a Day' RFI, May 2026)
ACC AMIC expeditionary air units (Deployable Tactical Communications RFI, 2026)

current_workflow: S6 writes the PACE plan for each echelon/net in an OPORD Annex H or spreadsheet before the mission; transport priorities are static and by-hand

Each transport is configured in its own tool: MANET radios (Silvus StreamCaster / Persistent MPU5 / L3Harris Falcon) in vendor managers or INB2, SATCOM terminals in the terminal vendor GUI, Starlink/pLEO in the provider app, private 5G in the core vendor console, crypto and routers separately
During operations a link degrades (jamming, terrain, movement, weather); the first indicator is usually user complaints (chat, voice, stalled COP/TAK sync) rather than an alert
A soldier diagnoses by checking consoles one by one or by radio call, then manually switches to the alternate transport: re-routes, re-keys, re-addresses, re-registers services
Applications (fires, COP, logistics, chat) re-sync or the data is re-entered by hand; some state is lost
Network status is transcribed into PowerPoint/Excel for the commander's update; spectrum deconfliction with S2/EW is done manually and after the fact
current_solution: Manual PACE plus a patchwork: CodeMettle INB2 (fielded battalion-and-below NetOps on the RAP-TR platform, monitoring tactical radios and waveforms); UNO/TNO prototypes (RII with CodeMettle, QinetiQ US, via the C5 consortium) for enterprise-to-tactical DODIN ops; Army 'Seeker' Auto-PACE software installed by PM Tactical Network to aggregate and fail over SATCOM/troposcatter/TRILOS/cellular links at higher echelons; vendor-native tools (Persistent Cloud Relay hub router, Silvus management, Anduril Lattice Mesh on Klas Voyager hardware); SD-WAN appliances; DARPA MINC research prototypes (Peraton Labs, BAE) for autonomous heterogeneous network control.
failure: No fielded, radio-vendor-agnostic controller at brigade and below that sees all transports (MANET from several vendors, pLEO, GEO, 5G, HF), measures per-link quality, and moves application flows by policy; Seeker-class Auto-PACE lives at the SATCOM/hub layer and does not reach into MANET vendors' management planes; INB2/UNO consolidate status views but do not automate failover across new commercial transports; each vendor fix (Persistent, Anduril/Klas, Silvus) re-creates single-vendor lock-in; DDIL-tolerant status collection and automated status reporting remain manual.

evidence.claim: The Army's own UNO program goal is to 'simplify and reduce the number of network management tools' G6s/S6s use to manage and defend the tactical network and to ease Signal Soldier workload - a direct government statement of the tool-sprawl pain.
evidence.source_title: PEO C3T I2S - Unified Network Operations (UNO)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: UNO has been procured repeatedly in pieces: RFIs for a multiple-award IDIQ (2023-2024, PdM TCNO), OTA prototypes through the C5 consortium (QinetiQ US award reported 2024-12-30; RII prime with CodeMettle Phase II subcontract 2025-10) - and the MA IDIQ award itself could not be confirmed as of 2026-09 (Public evidence insufficient).
evidence.source_title: QinetiQ US Awarded OTA to Support Unified Network Operation (UNO) Prototypes (ASDNews); CodeMettle UNO OT Phase II subcontract (PRNewswire)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Battalion-and-below NetOps already has an incumbent product: CodeMettle INB2 is 'currently fielded and deployed as part of the RAP-TR program' and the Army posted a May-2025 sources-sought/solicitation for Army-wide enterprise licenses and PDSS, alongside a notice of intent to synopsize CodeMettle INB2 software (i.e., sole-source intent). The single-pane half of G10 is therefore incumbent-held, not empty.
evidence.source_title: INB2 PEO C3N PM I2S solicitation (SAM mirror, 30-May-2025) and 'Notice of intent to synopsize CodeMettle INB2 software'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: PM Tactical Network installed an Auto-PACE software capability called 'Seeker' during its HT/LL multi-orbit SATCOM assessment: it aggregates links, detects outages quickly and self-heals, merging satellite, troposcatter, TRILOS and cellular transports. This shows automated PACE exists at the SATCOM/hub layer (vendor of Seeker not identified in retrieved snippets), but it is not described as reaching MANET vendors' management planes or brigade-and-below radios.
evidence.source_title: Multi-orbit SATCOM to boost Army network resiliency, capability in Large Scale Combat Operations (army.mil article 274494)
evidence.pub_date: unknown (2024 inferred from article number; not re-verified)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army network strategy has explicitly called for 'multi-path transport-agnostic' capabilities and 'automated agnostic transport diversity' since late 2022 - the requirement pre-dates NGC2 and has persisted for ~4 years without a fielded cross-vendor solution at brigade and below.
evidence.source_title: Army network plan will offset contested comms with multi-path transport-agnostic capabilities (Breaking Defense); Army using Europe and Pacific operational landscapes as 'laboratories' to enhance network resiliency (army.mil)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: PC-C6 (July 2026), the division-scale NGC2 validation, produced overheating hardware, incomplete data displays and 'semi-frequent connectivity drops'; the Army said some components would be cut - transport reliability remained a live problem at the end of the prototyping phase.
evidence.source_title: Army NGC2 to start scaling parts to more units (DefenseScoop)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DARPA's MINC program exists precisely to replace 'manual, static configuration of individual tactical networks' with software that autonomously configures networks-of-networks regardless of device, via a single secure SDN control overlay; Peraton Labs held a contract worth up to $20M over 42 months (reported completion ~Feb 2025) and BAE Systems was also a performer. Transition to a program of record: Public evidence insufficient.
evidence.source_title: MINC | DARPA; Peraton Labs secures contract under DARPA's MINC programme (Army Technology)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Second and third buyers voice the same need: USSOCOM's TACLAN/SDN 'King for a Day' RFI (posted 2026-05-15) asks for a modular C2 network with edge compute, SD-WAN and EW resilience; ACC AMIC's Deployable Tactical Communications RFI (responses due 2026-02-25) asks for routing, edge compute and application-level QoS in contested forward environments.
evidence.source_title: USSOCOM TACLAN and SDN 'King for a Day' RFI (GovDash mirror); ACC AMIC Deployable Tactical Communications RFI (SAM.gov)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DIU's ORIENT project (connect robust long-haul comms to redundant local mesh so ADA2 systems keep operating in disconnected, disrupted, low-bandwidth, intermittent environments) drew 130 proposals from 119 companies; DIU awarded prototype OTs to Viasat, Aalyria, Higher Ground and IoT/AI on 2024-11-20 - a prototype award, not deployment.

evidence.claim: Money exists but is prime-channelled: FY2026 NGC2 request included ~$1.36B for the C2 Transport layer (RDT&E+Procurement) within ~$3B-3.3B total; FY27 NGC2 request ~$3.78B; the FY26 NDAA capped obligation at 50% pending a report and the HASC FY27 mark would cut $710M. GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20) found the Army lacks a life-cycle cost estimate despite ~$3.3B identified through FY2026.

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Exercise reporting shows the multi-transport reality: at PC-C6 L3Harris radios formed part of the transport layer with 'PACE communications planning options' (vendor account); at Lightning Surge (25th ID, 2026-04) private 5G carried the call-for-fire path for the first time and 'tyranny of distance' drove transport choices - PACE is still 'planning options', i.e., human-executed, per the vendor's own wording.
evidence.source_title: A Collaborative Capstone: L3Harris at Project Convergence (L3Harris editorial, 2026-08); Accelerating transformative technologies aids commanders' readiness across the Pacific (army.mil 2026-04-21)

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons. (1) The management planes a controller needs are owned by radio vendors (Silvus/Motorola, Persistent, L3Harris, TrellisWare) who monetise their own controllers and, for PoR radios, sit behind Type-1 crypto and ITAR technical data; startups without radios, clearances and U.S.-person staff cannot even collect the telemetry. (2) The buyer has already chosen owners for each half: CodeMettle INB2 is the fielded battalion-and-below NetOps product with a 2025 sole-source-style license/PDSS action, UNO/TNO prototypes went to RII/CodeMettle and QinetiQ US through the C5 consortium, Seeker-style Auto-PACE is run by PM Tactical Network, and NGC2 transport is integrated by Anduril (now owning Klas) and Lockheed teams - the Army's stated preference is for the team lead to own integration. (3) Prior attempts stalled in prototype purgatory: DARPA MINC (Peraton, BAE) has no public transition, DIU ORIENT awardees (Aalyria, Viasat, Higher Ground, IoT/AI) hold prototype OTs, and the UNO MA IDIQ promised for 2025-2026 still cannot be confirmed - accreditation of anything in the encrypted path (CSfC/ATO) and exercise-slot scarcity slow every entrant to program timelines.
technical_wedge: Not the orchestrator itself (incumbent-held) but the missing open glue beneath it: a radio-agnostic transport telemetry and policy adapter layer - a small Linux/container agent on the existing edge box that speaks each transport's northbound interface (SNMP/REST/CLI for MANET radios and SATCOM modems, Starlink and 5G CPE APIs, HF ALE controllers), normalises per-link latency/loss/jitter/RSSI/SNR into one open schema, evaluates a declarative 'PACE-as-code' policy, and exposes NGC2-style non-proprietary APIs that INB2/TNO, Lattice Mesh or an SD-WAN can consume. Sold as a component to UNO/NGC2 teams and as a DDIL-tolerant telemetry/store-and-forward collector with auto-generated network status reporting for S6 cells. A second, lower-risk variant is the DDIL network emulation/test harness the Army is already funding through SBIR (Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network topic), which needs no ITAR radio data.

mvp.what: Container-based transport telemetry + PACE policy agent with adapters for four commercial transports (Doodle Labs or Rajant mesh radio, Starlink terminal, a private 5G CPE, an HF ALE modem or a second mesh), a per-flow path-selection policy engine, a DDIL-tolerant local time-series store that syncs when connected, and a browser HMI that renders link health and an auto-generated network status slide; TAK/CoT and a video stream as the applications.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: 8-10 node field test on commercial hardware with induced degradation (attenuators, antenna shading, vehicle movement, RF interference within FCC rules) showing sub-second detection and automated flow migration versus manual switching, with published telemetry schema and adapter SDK; plus a network-emulation mode replaying recorded link traces.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That a vendor-agnostic adapter layer can be written against public/commercial interfaces without vendor cooperation, that automated failover measurably beats manual PACE on time-to-recover and packet loss, that it runs inside a 100-200 W edge box footprint, and that a signal NCO can author policy without the vendor - and, critically, that at least one PoR radio vendor or NGC2/UNO team is willing to expose a northbound interface.

data_requirement.what: Per-link telemetry (latency, loss, jitter, throughput, RSSI/SNR, neighbor tables) from each transport; realistic tactical traffic profiles (TAK/CoT, VoIP, video, fires messages); recorded link-outage traces from movement/jamming; spectrum plans and PACE plans (typically CUI); management-interface documentation for PoR radios (ITAR-controlled for many).
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Commercial-radio telemetry (Doodle Labs, Rajant, Starlink, 5G CPE, HF ALE) is obtainable by purchase and public docs. PoR radio management docs (Silvus, Persistent, L3Harris Falcon) generally require NDAs, U.S.-person handling and often ITAR licensing - a non-U.S.-person founder cannot lawfully receive that technical data without an export authorization; needs export counsel. Real jamming performance and Army spectrum/PACE plans are CUI or classified and are not obtainable pre-award; use synthetic traces and open network emulators.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily. Anduril now owns both the NGC2 data-layer baseline and, via Klas, the edge network box; Lattice Mesh already claims multi-path data distribution and Anduril could expose a PACE policy layer as a Lattice feature. L3Harris and GDMS own PoR radio management planes and could extend them across transports. Motorola/Silvus and Persistent can extend proprietary controllers. CodeMettle/RII can add automation to INB2/TNO under existing UNO OTAs. None needs a startup's help to do it.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Mostly REJECT as a standalone company. The only defensible startup position is a neutral, open adapter/telemetry layer that vendors will not build because it commoditises their controllers - and that neutrality is exactly what incumbents and the buyer's prime-led model do not reward. A narrow win is possible only if CPE C2IN enforces its 'government-approved non-proprietary API' rule on the transport layer and buys the adapter layer separately, or if a second buyer (USSOCOM, ACC AMIC, an ally) wants freedom from the Army stack; neither is evidenced yet.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Software that manages military radios and encrypted transports touches ITAR technical data (radio management interfaces, waveform behaviour), CUI (network and spectrum plans), RMF/ATO on DODIN-A, potential NSA CSfC requirements, and usually SIPR-level integration requiring facility and personnel clearances. Commercial-hardware MVPs avoid most of this until the first PoR integration, after which the burden arrives all at once.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot receive ITAR technical data without an export license, cannot hold a security clearance, and can trigger FOCI mitigation if holding significant ownership or control; SBIR requires >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership. These are constraints to design around with export, immigration and government-contracts counsel, not a definitive legal judgment here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Multi-transport failover and single-pane monitoring have commercial analogues in public safety (FirstNet + LMR + satellite), mining/energy (Rajant-class mesh + LTE + SATCOM), maritime and disaster response, and commercial SD-WAN already solves the wired/cellular/SATCOM version. The specifically military parts (MANET vendor adapters, PACE-as-code, EW awareness, DDIL reporting) have a thin commercial market, so dual-use exists for the platform but not for the differentiating features.

defensibility.explanation: The adapter library for many radios/terminals and its accreditation footprint are the only durable assets; algorithms for path selection are well known (MINC, SD-WAN). Telemetry datasets from exercises could become valuable for DDIL emulation but are typically government-owned. Defensibility is weak against vendors who own the interfaces.

why_now: Since 2023: commercial pLEO became a fielded Army transport (pLEO IDIQ 2023, ceiling raised to $13B Oct 2024, SpaceX SDN Backbone $2.29B May 2026); private 5G carried a live call-for-fire path at Lightning Surge (2026-04) and a simulated M777 mission at C5ISR Center (2026-05); NGC2 codified a distinct transport layer with government-approved non-proprietary APIs and moved from prototype OTAs (July/Sept 2025) to baseline fielding to I Corps and III Armored Corps (2026-09); UNO moved to OTA prototypes (2024-12, 2025-10) and INB2 was re-competed as a license/PDSS action (2025-05); PC-C6 still logged semi-frequent connectivity drops (2026-07). The multi-transport problem now exists at scale for the first time, but the buyer is simultaneously locking in who solves it.
killer_risk: The slot is already taken and gated: CodeMettle INB2 (fielded, sole-source-style 2025 action) and the RII/CodeMettle/QinetiQ UNO prototypes own NetOps; PM Tactical Network already runs Seeker Auto-PACE; Anduril (with Klas) and Lockheed own NGC2 transport integration and the Army wants team leads to own integration; radio vendors own the APIs and have every incentive to keep them closed. A two-founder team with one non-U.S.-person founder cannot legally access the ITAR radio data needed to build cross-vendor adapters, so the MVP would be confined to commercial radios that the Army does not field at scale - producing a demo the buyer cannot use.

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling with allies, for a specific reason: allied land forces (Germany D-LBO/TaWAN LBO with Rheinmetall/blackned, UK LE TacCIS/TRINITY, Nordic Bittium framework, Japan ATLA mobile comms prototype) are each buying new multi-transport tactical networks in 2025-2029 and are less locked to U.S. radio vendors, so a radio-agnostic adapter layer has more open interfaces to work against, and a German founder has a natural route into the Bundeswehr ecosystem (blackned, Rheinmetall) where ITAR does not gate the commercial radios used. Counterpoints: the allied 'integration layer' slot is also incumbent-held (Rheinmetall/blackned, Systematic, Thales), coalition interoperability is measured at CWIX/Bold Quest around FMN standards rather than PACE automation, and allied budgets for NetOps software are smaller and slower. Net: allied extension improves feasibility of building the product (interface access) more than it improves the market size.
